title: Family, his teacher and a concert violinist
summary: His father died in 1922, relatives have moved away, and he recalls his teacher and one violin recital.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: I was gonna ask, how long?
I haven't been there now. See, my father died in 22. I haven't been there since.
1922. Oh, do you have any other relatives living there?
Not anymore. What few relatives we have left, they have moved to Seattle. A couple of cousins, retired school teachers, and my sister and brother, they've been here with me. Oh, any number of years.
Your teacher at the French Opera, you say he was the assistant conductor. Assistant conductor there.
Did he play an instrument too, sometimes?
He was violinist. Oh, the concertmaster. Oh, yeah.
I know a lot of times the concertmaster is the assistant conductor. Yeah. I didn't know if he just waved to the car.
Oh, he was a wonderful man. I shall always be thankful to him. He was marvelous.
Do you remember hearing any good concert violinists when you were a boy and a student there at that time? Did they give recitals in the French Opera too, or just opera?

Well, we didn't get too many of them, because of course you know what New Orleans was in those days. The only one I can remember very vividly, and it's this old man I told you about, B-Day, that this orchestra sent over there to study. And when he came, he made one trip after he was a grown man and gave one recital.
And I played in the orchestra that was on the program. At that time I had developed enough to play in the orchestra. That played.
